Response Primitives Api Admin Primitives Get

BeatManifest.title: BeatManifest
BeatManifest.description: One rendered beat. Times are seconds from the start of the beat's own video.

BeatRenderSpec.title: BeatRenderSpec
BeatRenderSpec.description: One beat to render: a primitive, its validated parameters and its narration.

BranchChoiceEvent.title: BranchChoiceEvent
BranchChoiceEvent.description: The option selected at a branch point after the module (§5.6.4).

BranchOption.title: BranchOption
BranchOption.description: A branch offered after the module, described by its own scene plan (§5.6.4).

BranchPoint.title: BranchPoint
BranchPoint.description:
The choice after a module (§5.6.4, Fig. 4.5). With no answer in time, the default is
taken.

CheckItem.title: CheckItem
CheckItem.description:
A bank item as the student sees it: never with its answer (§5.7.3).

Text may contain inline LaTeX between `$` signs, which the frontend renders with KaTeX.

CheckQuestionPatch.title: CheckQuestionPatch
CheckQuestionPatch.description: Changed fields only. The item is checked again as a whole after the change.

ChipInterval.title: ChipInterval
ChipInterval.description: When a concept chip is shown beside the video, within its beat (§5.6.2).

ChipViewEvent.title: ChipViewEvent
ChipViewEvent.description: Selecting a concept chip to read its definition (§5.6.2).

CurrentModule.title: CurrentModule
CurrentModule.description:
What the player should do now.

- `ready`: play `module` from the variant `cache_key` (at least its first beat is ready).
- `preparing`: wait for the stream; `stage` says how far generation has got.
- `failed`: show `failure`, then call `finish` for the module to move on.
- `complete`: the lesson is over.

DiagnosticState.title: DiagnosticState
DiagnosticState.description: The onboarding diagnostic (UC 4.2): at most five items, resumable.

GlossaryDefinition.title: GlossaryDefinition
GlossaryDefinition.description: What the chip overlay shows (§5.6.2, UC 4.5). The definition may contain `$…$` math.

ImLostReplay.title: ImLostReplay
ImLostReplay.description: At Level 1: replay the beat with its chips open (§5.6.3).

ImLostSubstitute.title: ImLostSubstitute
ImLostSubstitute.description: The module continues one level lower from the start of `resume_beat_index` (§5.6.3).

InteractionEventBatch.title: InteractionEventBatch
InteractionEventBatch.description: The body of one request from the player's event logger.

LessonStatus.title: LessonStatus
LessonStatus.description: LESSON.status: in progress, completed, or abandoned.

Level.description:
The three renderings of every micro-module.

The levels differ in how much of the explanation is shown and how quickly it is delivered,
not in what is taught. Level 2 is the reference level.
Level.title: Level

ModuleEnd.title: ModuleEnd
ModuleEnd.description: Returned when a module ends: its check items (§5.7.3) and its branch point, if any.

ModuleFailure.title: ModuleFailure
ModuleFailure.description: Why a module could not be prepared, and what replaces it (§6.4.6).

ModuleManifest.title: ModuleManifest
ModuleManifest.description:
The segment manifest of one rendered variant (§5.4.4).

The Interactive Playback Layer uses it to time the chips, locate beat boundaries, and
attribute each interaction to the concepts of its beat. A variant is identified by its
cache key, so the same manifest serves every module that reuses the variant.

After an "I'm Lost" press a variant may hold only beats j onward; it is complete once all
`beat_count` beats are present.

ModuleRenderRequest.title: ModuleRenderRequest
ModuleRenderRequest.description: Render one module at one level (§5.3.4).

ModuleStyle.title: ModuleStyle
ModuleStyle.description:
MODULE.style: theory, worked example, or default.

Theory and worked example are the two branch options a scene plan can offer (§5.6.4).

OutOfScope.title: OutOfScope
OutOfScope.description: The query is outside the supported topics (UC 4.3, alternative flow).

PauseEvent.title: PauseEvent
PauseEvent.description:
A pause, sent when playback resumes. A dwell longer than a set threshold is evidence of
difficulty (Table 5.4); the threshold belongs to the Learner State Module.

Position.title: Position
Position.description: Where the student is in a lesson. `position_s` is seconds into the beat's own video.

PrimitiveAdmin.title: PrimitiveAdmin
PrimitiveAdmin.description:
A primitive's metadata. Its code arrives by pull request and must pass the validation
harness (§5.3.2), so the admin manages only status and description.

RenderStatus.title: RenderStatus
RenderStatus.description: MODULE.render_status: queued, rendering, ready, or failed.

RewindEvent.title: RewindEvent
RewindEvent.description: Seeking back to an earlier point. Evidence for the concepts of the beat returned to.

ScenePlan.title: ScenePlan
ScenePlan.description:
The plan of one micro-module (Table 5.1).

A scene plan carries no difficulty level: the same plan is rendered at every level, and the
segment list fixes the number and order of segments for every variant (§5.2.3). Unknown
fields such as "level" are rejected.

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description: One segment (a "beat" in Chapter 6) of a micro-module.

SpeedChangeEvent.title: SpeedChangeEvent
SpeedChangeEvent.description: Lowering or raising the playback speed (Table 5.4: slowed is difficulty, sped up is ease).

StepTiming.title: StepTiming
StepTiming.description: When a step runs within its beat, and the passage spoken over it.

BeatReady.description: A beat is stored and can be played. Playback starts when the first beat is ready.
BeatReady.title: BeatReady

GenerationProgress.description: Which stage of generation a module has reached, so the interface can show progress.
GenerationProgress.title: GenerationProgress

ModuleFailed.description:
Generation failed after its retries (§6.4.6).

A module whose plan cannot be validated is replaced by a cached variant of the same concept
or, failing that, by the glossary definition; `fallback` says which, if either.
ModuleFailed.title: ModuleFailed

ModuleReady.description: Every beat of the module is ready at this level.
ModuleReady.title: ModuleReady
